etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: Shortened from tawdry lace; originally a corruption and rebracketing of Saint Audrey lace (from Old English Æðelþrȳð). The lace necklaces sold to pilgrims to Saint Audrey fell out of fashion in the 17th century, and so tawdry was reinterpreted as meaning “cheap” or “vulgar”.
senses: (obsolete) Anything gaudy and cheap; pretentious finery. [17th–19th c.]
Of clothing, appearance, etc., cheap and gaudy; showy.
Of a character, behavior, or situation, etc., unseemly, base, mean-spirited, shameful.
